summary: Unexpected spike on March invoice attributed to embeddings usage — meter/billing clarification
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a large unexpected charge on their March invoice that they believe is due to embeddings usage out of pattern. Impact: Customer-facing billing dispute; finance needs clarification before sending payment. Environment: Production (us-east-1) under enterprise account Novara Health; Dedicated plan with reserved capacity token bucket. Customer says their app did not change during the billing window.

Initial claim: Novara Health observed a 7x month-over-month increase in embeddings token usage between 2026-02-25 and 2026-03-01 triggering overage charges. They attached a CSV of per-route metric counts and a screenshot of the invoice line items.

Requested outcome: Provide a breakdown of what drove the usage spike, confirm whether any metering policy or rate-limit misattribution occurred, and issue credits if overcounting is confirmed.

Steps to reproduce (from support POV):
1) Pull invoices for account novara@novara-health.com for Feb and Mar 2026 from billing system.
2) Query metering logs for embeddings.generate metrics for account id 107243 across 2026-02-20 to 2026-03-05 (token counts, request ids, model names).
3) Cross-reference with gateway logs for 429/5xx and retry bursts and with console rollout events.

Logs & artifacts provided by customer: CSV: novara_embeddings_usage_2026_02-20_03-05.csv (per-route token counts), invoice_screenshot_march.png (invoice snippet), support-ticket-export.txt (application logs timestamps).
steps_to_reproduce: Support steps: 1) Validate invoice line items; 2) Aggregate embeddings token usage in billing pipeline by token_type and model id during disputed window; 3) Check for double-counting incidents in the metering pipeline (duplicate insert from collector/service restarts); 4) Inspect gateway logs for replayed requests and for spikes of 5xx followed by client retry bursts; 5) Verify that reserved capacity billing rules were applied correctly (dedicated vs overage).
investigation_notes:
2026-03-12 10:34 — Initial triage by Billing: invoice line shows embedding tokens 11,732,450 for March (vs 1,532,110 in Feb).
2026-03-12 14:02 — Metering team: ran aggregation; raw token totals in metering DB match invoice totals. No obvious off-by-one.
2026-03-12 16:45 — Runtime team: noticed multiple repeated requests from a single client API key (key ending in -9f2) within a short window on 2026-02-27 03:12 UTC; timestamps show high retry count with 200 responses.
2026-03-13 09:10 — Hypothesis A: client-side misconfiguration caused duplicated calls (webhook retry + background job). Hypothesis B: collector-side duplicate ingestion after an autoscaling event caused re-ingestion of previously-seen events for a 20-minute window.
2026-03-13 11:00 — Queried collector offsets: found a blocked commit window during 03:10-03:30 UTC on 2026-02-27 where a lag and subsequent bulk commit re-emitted ~4.9M embedding tokens. This aligns with traffic spike.
2026-03-13 13:20 — Cross-check with customer: they confirmed a deploy of search indexer on 2026-02-27 which started a catch-up job that called embeddings in batch mode. They said this job was expected but they believed it to be within normal quota.
2026-03-13 15:45 — Billing to quantify which portion is attributable to expected activity vs platform double-counting. Currently estimating ~3.8M tokens of the disputed 10.2M look attributable to platform-side duplicate ingestion behavior; remainder appears to be customer-initiated catch-up.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-14 10:00 — Agreed outcome with customer: issue is mixed. We will issue a goodwill credit of $5,200.00 to offset the portion attributable to duplicate ingestion caused by collector bulk re-emission. Customer accepts and will pay the remaining balance. Follow-up actions: 1) Engineering to add deduplication window in collector for bulk commits (ticket INT-412); 2) Billing to apply $5,200.00 credit on March invoice and confirm via updated invoice PDF; 3) Support to update runbook to include a check for bulk-commit replays during billing disputes. Credit applied on 2026-03-14 and updated invoice generated.
